ja: 自己紹介しなきゃね。
en: I should introduce myself.
alternatives: I need to introduce myself.
I have to introduce myself.
I'd better introduce myself.
point: 「〜しなきゃ」は should か have to

ja: 私の肩書きは名ばかりとも言える。
en: My title is, shall we say, nominal.
alternatives: You could say my title is in name only.
My title is more nominal than substantive, I'd say.
point: shall we say は少し含みを持たせて言葉を選ぶ。

ja: 移住してなければ、今ここにいない。
en: If I hadn't emigrated, I wouldn't be here.
alternatives: Had I not emigrated, I wouldn't be here.
I wouldn't be here if I hadn't emigrated.
point: 過去の事実が今に響く。if 節は had、結果は would be

ja: 私は出版でずっと修業してます。
en: I've been cutting my teeth in publishing.
alternatives: I've been learning the ropes in publishing.
I've been getting my start in publishing.
point: cut my teeth は初めの実務経験を積むこと。

ja: 私が型に従えば居場所は見つからなかった。
en: Had I conformed, I'd never have found my niche.
alternatives: If I'd conformed, I wouldn't have found my niche.
I'd never have found my place had I conformed.
point: find my niche は自分に合う役割や居場所を見つける。

ja: 作ったの君だって、ミカが言ってた。
en: Mika said you're the one who made this.
alternatives: Mika said it was you who made this.
Mika told me you made this.
point: said の中に the one who の節。時制は文脈で選ぶ

ja: 私が重役と付き合う機会は稀だ。
en: Seldom do I rub shoulders with executives.
alternatives: I rarely mingle with executives.
I seldom mix with senior executives.
point: rub shoulders with は人と交流すること。

ja: 私は音楽が好き。
en: I like music.
alternatives: I enjoy music.
Music appeals to me.
point: music は数えないので a をつけない。

ja: あなたの原動力を伺えますか？
en: May I ask what makes you tick?
alternatives: Could you tell me what drives you?
May I ask what really motivates you?
point: what makes you tick は行動や関心の原動力を尋ねる表現。

ja: 私を雇ったのは、ミカさんです。
en: It was Mika who hired me.
alternatives: Mika is the one who hired me.
Mika was the person who hired me.
point: It was 人 who で「〜なのは」を強調

ja: 私は大阪出身の設計士です。
en: I'm an architect from Osaka.
alternatives: I'm an architect who's from Osaka.
I'm an Osaka-born architect.
point: 「〜出身の」は名詞の後ろに from を置く

ja: ここに惹かれたのは、人の温かさ。
en: What drew me here was the people's warmth.
alternatives: It was the people's warmth that drew me here.
The warmth of the people is what drew me here.
point: What ~ was で一番の理由を強調

ja: ここで働いて三年になります。
en: I've worked here for three years.
alternatives: I've been working here for three years.
I've been at this company for three years.
point: 「今まで続く期間」は現在完了 + for

ja: そこに私の妹がいる。
en: There's my younger sister.
alternatives: My younger sister's there.
That's my little sister.
point: There's でそこにいる人を指し示す。

ja: 弊社はこの分野で有名です。
en: We're well known in this field.
alternatives: Our company is well known in this field.
Our firm is well known in this industry.
point: 受動態 be well known in ~

ja: 私が避けた分野は今では得意分野だ。
en: The field I avoided is now my forte.
alternatives: What I avoided is now my strong suit.
The field I avoided is now my specialty.
point: forte は得意分野。避けた過去と得意な現在を対比する。

ja: ミカが君は会うべき人だと言っていた。
en: Mika told me you're someone I should meet.
alternatives: Mika said you're someone I should meet.
Mika said I should meet you.
point: you're someone (that) I should meet の入れ子

ja: 型にはめられたくなくて肩書きを避ける。
en: I avoid job titles to resist being pigeonholed.
alternatives: I avoid titles because I dislike being pigeonholed.
I skip job titles to avoid being labeled.
point: to resist being pigeonholed は一つの型に当てはめられるのを避ける目的を表す。

ja: こちら営業部の田中です。
en: This is Tanaka from Sales.
alternatives: This is Tanaka in Sales.
I'm Tanaka from Sales.
point: 名詞の後ろに from + 部署で説明

ja: 緊張すると私は黙り込む。
en: I clam up when nervous.
alternatives: I go quiet when I get nervous.
I stop talking when I feel nervous.
point: clam up は黙り込む。

ja: 私は先に挨拶すべき。
en: I should say hello first.
alternatives: I ought to say hello first.
I should give the first greeting.
point: should で先に挨拶するのがよいと伝える。

ja: ピアノが弾けます。
en: I can play piano.
alternatives: I can play the piano.
I'm able to play piano.
point: 「弾ける」は can + 動詞。楽器には the を付けても付けなくてもよい

ja: 大阪出身で、たこ焼き好きです。
en: Born in Osaka, I love takoyaki.
alternatives: As an Osaka native, I love takoyaki.
Being from Osaka, I love takoyaki.
Coming from Osaka, I love takoyaki.
point: 分詞構文では Born の前の being を省ける

ja: 君はどんな仕事してるの？
en: What's your line of work?
alternatives: What kind of work do you do?
What do you do for a living?
point: line of work は仕事の分野や職種。

ja: 私が名刺を渡していい？
en: May I give you my card?
alternatives: Can I offer my business card?
May I hand you my card?
point: May I give you my card? で相手に自分の名刺を渡す許可を求める。

ja: 私は姉より社交的だ。
en: I'm more outgoing than my sister.
alternatives: I'm more sociable than my sister.
My sister's less outgoing than me.
point: outgoing は人と気軽に交流する性格。

ja: もっと早く会えていればよかった。
en: I wish we had met earlier.
alternatives: If only we'd met sooner.
I wish we'd met sooner.
point: 過去の後悔は wish + 過去完了

ja: ケンって呼んでね。
en: Call me Ken.
alternatives: Just call me Ken.
You can call me Ken.
point: 「呼んで」は call me + 名前

ja: 会う前から、存じていました。
en: I'd heard of you before we met.
alternatives: I knew of you before we met.
I had known your name before we met.
point: 会う前のことなので過去完了

ja: 私の仕事は、企業向けの翻訳です。
en: What I do is translate for companies.
alternatives: My job is translating for companies.
What I do is business translation.
point: What I do is のあとは動詞の原形

ja: 自分を安売りする衝動を抑えればよかった。
en: I wish I'd resisted the urge to undersell myself.
alternatives: I wish I'd resisted the temptation to undersell myself.
If only I'd resisted the urge to undersell myself.
point: undersell myself は実力以下に自分を紹介する。

ja: 私は看護師です。
en: I'm a nurse.
alternatives: I work as a nurse.
I'm a nurse by profession.
point: 職業の前には a をつける

ja: 先月ここに越したばかりです。
en: I only moved here last month.
alternatives: I just moved here last month.
I've only lived here since last month.
point: last month があれば過去形、since なら現在完了

ja: 私は先生です。
en: I'm a teacher.
alternatives: I teach.
Teaching is my job.
point: 職業を言う単数の名詞は a teacher。

ja: 私は英語を勉強中。
en: I'm studying English.
alternatives: I'm learning English.
I'm working on my English.
point: am studying で現在勉強していることを伝える。

ja: 行ってなきゃ、会えなかったね。
en: If I hadn't gone, we'd never have met.
alternatives: If I hadn't gone, we wouldn't have met.
Had I not gone, we'd never have met.
point: 過去の仮定は If + had + 過去分詞、would have + 過去分詞

ja: 仕事で、出張ばかりさせられてる。
en: Work has me living out of suitcases.
alternatives: My job has me living out of a suitcase.
My job has me traveling constantly.
point: have + 人 + 〜ing で「〜させられている」状態を表す

ja: 不器用に見えても私は人の意図を察する。
en: Awkward though I seem, I read between the lines.
alternatives: Although I seem awkward, I pick up unspoken intentions.
I understand unstated intentions despite seeming awkward.
point: read between the lines は言葉に出ない意図を読み取る。

ja: 私の得意分野は言外の意味を読むこと。
en: What I do best is decipher what's left unsaid.
alternatives: My strength is understanding what people leave unspoken.
I'm best at interpreting what isn't explicitly said.
point: left unsaid は口にされないが含まれている意味。

ja: うちの課は十人います。
en: There are ten of us.
alternatives: Our team has ten people.
We're a team of ten.
point: 人数は there are ten of us と言える

ja: あなたも来るとケンが言ってた。
en: Ken said you'd be coming too.
alternatives: Ken told me you'd be coming too.
Ken mentioned you were coming too.
point: said の後は would。you'd は you would

ja: 私は海の近くで育った。
en: I grew up near the sea.
alternatives: I was raised near the ocean.
I grew up by the ocean.
point: grew up は grow up の過去形。

ja: 自分を型にはめるなら私は仲介役かな。
en: Were I to pigeonhole myself, I'd say mediator.
alternatives: If I had to categorize myself, I'd say mediator.
If I needed a label, I'd choose mediator.
point: pigeonhole は人を単純な一つの型に押し込める。

ja: 仕事で私は合わなそうな意見をまとめる。
en: My work has me reconciling seemingly irreconcilable positions.
alternatives: My job involves getting apparently incompatible viewpoints reconciled.
My work makes me reconcile seemingly incompatible positions.
point: have 人 doing は仕事でその役割を担うことを表す。

ja: 前に会ったかもしれませんね。
en: We might have met before.
alternatives: We may have met before.
I think we might have met before.
point: 過去の推量は might have + 過去分詞

ja: 出身は東京です。
en: I'm from Tokyo.
alternatives: I come from Tokyo.
Tokyo is my hometown.
point: 出身は be from で言う

ja: 人見知りでも話は好き。
en: Although I'm shy, I enjoy chatting.
alternatives: Though I'm shy, I like talking.
I'm shy, but I enjoy chatting.
point: although の節に but は重ねない

ja: 私は今年卒業する予定。
en: I'm graduating this year.
alternatives: I'm going to graduate this year.
I plan to graduate this year.
point: 予定の進行形で決まっている卒業を伝える。

ja: どちらのご出身か伺えますか？
en: May I ask where you're from?
alternatives: Would you mind telling me where you're from?
Could I ask where you're from?
point: 間接疑問は where you're from の語順

ja: お噂はかねがね伺っております。
en: I've heard a lot about you.
alternatives: I've heard so much about you.
I've heard great things about you.
point: 初対面の定番は現在完了 I've heard

ja: 私が転職してなければ今も型通りに働く。
en: Had I not changed jobs, I'd still work conventionally.
alternatives: Without changing jobs, I'd still be working conventionally.
I'd still work conventionally had I not changed jobs.
point: Had I not changed jobs は過去の転職がなかった場合と今も型通りに働く結果を結ぶ。

ja: 時間があれば、サーフを始めるのに。
en: If I had time, I'd take up surfing.
alternatives: I'd take up surfing if I had time.
If I had more time, I'd take up surfing.
point: 始める趣味は take up、仮定は had と would

ja: 加藤さんによろしくと頼まれた。
en: Kato asked me to say hi.
alternatives: Kato asked me to say hello.
Kato wanted me to say hi.
point: 「人に〜を頼む」は ask 人 to do

ja: 英語を学びに来ました。
en: I came to learn English.
alternatives: I'm here to learn English.
I came here to study English.
point: 目的は to + 動詞

ja: まあ、何でも屋みたいなものです。
en: I'm something of a jack-of-all-trades.
alternatives: You could say I'm a jack-of-all-trades.
I'm a bit of a jack-of-all-trades.
point: something of a 〜 で断定をやわらげる

ja: 料理なら少しできます。
en: I can cook a little.
alternatives: I can cook a bit.
I can cook a little bit.
point: a little で「少し」の控えめさが出る

ja: 分野を変え私は内部の常識を疑った。
en: Changing fields, I questioned what insiders take for granted.
alternatives: Changing fields made me question insiders' unexamined assumptions.
I challenged insiders' unquestioned assumptions when I changed fields.
point: take for granted は疑わず当然と思う。

ja: 来月、結婚するんです。
en: I'm getting married next month.
alternatives: I'll get married next month.
Next month I'm getting married.
point: 近い予定は現在進行形で言える

ja: 先日メールを差し上げた者です。
en: I'm the one who emailed you.
alternatives: I'm the person who emailed you.
I'm the one who sent you an email.
point: 人を説明する関係詞は who

ja: 週末は映画を観て過ごす。
en: I spend my weekends watching movies.
alternatives: I spend weekends watching movies.
I usually watch movies on weekends.
point: spend + 時間 + -ing で「〜して過ごす」

ja: 今は東京に住んでます。
en: I'm living in Tokyo.
alternatives: I live in Tokyo now.
Now I live in Tokyo.
point: 今の暮らしは進行形でも現在形でも言える
